summary: Frontend-only retest of the Montreal skyline watermark fix on the public Welcome page ('/'). Verified DOM presence, image src, network 200, computed opacity, rendered dimensions, non-blocking layering, and non-regression of foreground content (title, mode cards, Continuer navigation). All checks passed with zero console errors and zero failed network requests.
critical_code_review_comments: Welcome.jsx watermark uses `fixed inset-0` inside a parent with `overflow-hidden`; this renders correctly in Chromium but a `position: absolute` container (or moving the fixed layer outside the overflow-hidden wrapper) would be more spec-safe across engines. Non-blocking observation only.

The watermark has no width/height or loading attributes; the 305 KB webp is fetched on first paint of the public landing page. Consider loading="lazy"/decoding="async" or a smaller variant for LCP on slow connections.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 2 covered ONLY the Welcome page watermark fix. Measured values on 1920x1080: watermark div (data-testid='montreal-watermark') z-index 0, pointer-events none; naturalSize 2000x1500, HTTP 200 image/webp, computed opacity 0.4, rendered 1920x594 occupying the viewport lower half (top=486, bottom=1080). elementFromPoint at (50%,80%) returned foreground content DIV, confirming the watermark does not intercept clicks. Mode cards toggle the Continuer label (SOLO/PRO) and Continuer navigates to /register. Auth/dossiers/modules/PDF were validated in iteration_1 and were not re-tested.
rca_of_the_issue: Original 'Je ne vois rien' bug was caused by an over-attenuated watermark whose subject fell below the fold. Current implementation (h-[55%], object-bottom, opacity-40 with a white top gradient) makes the skyline clearly visible in the lower half of the viewport at both scroll-top and scroll-bottom positions — confirmed visually via screenshots. Fix is effective.
